title: BTP security & admin starter pack
summary: Who can do what: admins, members, identity, roles, destinations — the controls beginners must not skip.
explain:
Security and admin on BTP are about control planes and data planes.

Admin control plane:
• Who is global account admin vs subaccount admin vs space developer.
• Entitlements: who can enable expensive services.
• Members: least privilege for humans.

Identity & access:
• Users authenticate (IAS / IdP concepts).
• Apps get roles/scopes (XSUAA patterns).
• Destinations carry how apps call other systems (auth type, audience).
• Principal propagation keeps the human identity for audit.

Golden beginner rules:
1) Separate prod subaccounts and prod admins.
2) Never Admin.All for convenience.
3) Destinations and secrets are security artifacts.
4) Authn ≠ authz — login success can still be 403.
5) Test negative paths (wrong tenant, missing scope).
analogy: Building security: keys to the building (admin), badges for rooms (roles), sealed courier bags between buildings (destinations), and cameras (audit).
whyItMatters: Most production incidents in early BTP projects are mis-admins, open roles, or broken identity hops — not exotic zero-days.
formalPoints: Split admin duties by stage and blast radius
Authn proves identity; authz grants action rights
Destinations and secrets are first-class security config
Least privilege and negative tests are mandatory
commonMistakes: Technical user with god rights for ‘propagation later’
Putting secrets in code or tickets
howToRecognize: Landing zone setup, first Fiori app to CAP call, partner integration design
howToApply: Write an admin RACI for global vs subaccount
List scopes for one approve action — none should be Admin.All
mnemonic: KEYS ≠ BADGES: Admin keys open buildings; scopes/badges open rooms. Never master-key everyone.
useCases: Greenfield design workshop: decide if “BTP security & admin starter pack” is required given constraints (latency, clean-core, team skills).
Incident bridge: symptoms appear; use “BTP security & admin starter pack” to classify the failing hop before changing config.
Architecture review board: defend why you accepted residual risk around “BTP security & admin starter pack”.

designTradeoffs.optionA: Central IdP + token validation at every edge
designTradeoffs.risk: Local stores fragment identity and weaken IR

designTradeoffs.whenChooseB: Never in prod — only throwaway sandboxes

designTradeoffs.optionA: Server-side tenant predicate on every query
designTradeoffs.risk: UI filters are not a security boundary
